note: An instructive edge case that fails the ICP by being past it rather than short of it. Income holds: 'The price doesn't really shock me, to be honest. It's something that I would expect' in response to a four-figure indication, and he absorbed $2,000/year without resistance. Good-to-great is his own framing — 'I think I'm above average already, but I just want to push it a little bit more.' Not deconditioned is emphatic: four structured strength sessions a week for three years, twenty years of competitive football, tracks his loads. But neglected_health fails as the criterion is written. Health is not the area he has let slide; it is the area he already manages, alongside a physiotherapist, and he says so plainly — 'it's not that deep that I don't feel good at the moment... It doesn't impact my life negatively at the moment.' The stated ICP assumes a gap between success and health that this prospect does not have, which is precisely why the six-month transformation had nothing to sell him and the rep routed him to a lower tier instead. 'Successful' is deliberately recorded in neither list: occupation was never asked, and 'I have a busy job' is all the transcript contains, so the criterion is untested rather than failed.
